editorial.headline: A Sharia Pension Activity That Remains Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity administers Sharia-based defined-contribution pension programmes for individuals, from employees to independent workers.
editorial.body:
This is the administration of Sharia-based pension funds operated through financial institutions. Its focus is a defined-contribution pension programme for individuals: employees as well as independent workers. The programme is distinct from the employer pension fund maintained for employees of the relevant bank or life-insurance company. In practical terms, the activity concerns the stewardship of an individual pension arrangement structured around Sharia principles, rather than an employer’s own pension fund.

The record places the activity within every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth matters because the scope is not framed as a narrow institutional back-office function. It is an activity directed at individual participants, including people whose working lives sit inside conventional employment and those working independently, while preserving separation from the employer pension arrangement associated with the bank or life-insurance company concerned.

At the national level, foreign investment is allowed for this activity and foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is an unqualified national ownership ceiling in the record, not a partial foreign-investment allowance. A foreign-owned business considering this activity therefore has a clear national reading: the activity is open and the stated ceiling is full foreign ownership.

Bali’s position is also open on the record before us. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk across the island. For this activity, however, the Bali assessment states that its OSS risk at the Large scale is Medium-High or High, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The distinction is important: Bali’s result is not an exception invented around the national rule, but a direct consequence of the recorded risk treatment. On the available record, a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this activity is also not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
